crucialFeats: regenerated eye damage in combat time
converted the Teen Titans into Dark Titans

dossier.advantage: Heart of Darkness and dark immortality. The condensed evil of a hundred galaxies grants him near-infinite magical resources and the ability to instantly regenerate from the very essence of darkness.
dossier.mentality: A sadistic tyrant aiming for total conquest. He doesn't seek a challenge but revels in despair and the slow breaking of the opponent's spirit before their final annihilation.
dossier.quote: In seeking to eradicate my evil... You have made me supreme! I am now power. I am now death. I am now TRIGON!
dossier.style: Static dominance and devastating energy projection. Trigon utilizes his six eyes for hellfire blasts and his divine brute force to effortlessly smash any opponent.

fighterA.name: Character A

powers: Demonic energy projection, corruption, possession, regeneration, dimensional travel.
weaknesses: Peak control is strongest inside favorable demonic environments.
Broad cosmic resistance can slow his corruption tempo in neutral space.

crucialFeats: destroyed at least three solar systems while still weakened
withstood Agamotto in Agamotto's own realm
imprisoned Silver Surfer on Earth with an undetectable barrier
defeated Sphinx by locking him into an eternal time loop

dossier.advantage: Absolute power absorption and the Ultimate Nullifier. He can absorb energy directed against him (even from gods) and, if necessary, use the Nullifier to erase entire galaxies or timelines from existence.
dossier.mentality: A detached, eternally hungry force of nature. He feels no hatred or anger – he perceives heroes and deities like insects or fuel, acting entirely outside the categories of good and evil.
dossier.quote: Of all the creatures in the vastness of the universe, there is none like me. I was present at the birth of the universe, and I shall be there at its end.
dossier.style: Direct Power Cosmic dominance. Galactus strikes with devastating energy blasts, immobilizes enemies with telekinesis, and uses molecular restructuring to turn opponents into pure energy with a single gesture.

fighterB.name: Character B

powers: Power Cosmic, transmutation, large-scale energy projection, barriers, and matter control.
weaknesses: In low-fed states, response speed and margin for error decrease.

fight-simulation.opening: Trigon tries to convert the first exchange into corruption, possession pressure, and anti-symmetry.
fight-simulation.mid_fight: Galactus answers with scale stabilization, barrier control, and energy economy instead of respecting Trigon's preferred rules.
fight-simulation.late_fight: The finish depends on whether the battlefield stays toxic and demonic or gets normalized into something Galactus can metabolize.
fight-simulation.end_condition: If Galactus cannot normalize the battlefield, domain logic itself starts tilting the matchup toward Trigon.
fight-simulation.phase_1_event: Trigon tries to convert the first exchange into corruption, possession pressure, and anti-symmetry.
fight-simulation.phase_2_event: Galactus answers with scale stabilization, barrier control, and energy economy instead of respecting Trigon's preferred rules.
fight-simulation.phase_2_branch_a: The battlefield keeps sliding toward demonic logic and reinforces Trigon's edge.
fight-simulation.phase_2_branch_b: Galactus normalizes space and rebuilds the energy economy on his side.
fight-simulation.phase_3_event: The finish depends on whether the battlefield stays toxic and demonic or gets normalized into something Galactus can metabolize.
fight-simulation.phase_3_branch_a: Starvation and a toxic realm strip Galactus of the clean normalization route.
fight-simulation.phase_3_branch_b: Galactus turns the battlefield into fuel and restores his own scale logic.

final-summary.line_1: Galactus owns the paper comparison, 92.67 vs 87.33.
final-summary.line_2: Trigon stays dangerous when corruption and field logic replace normal combat symmetry.
final-summary.line_3: Starvation and home-realm control are the two conditions that let Trigon flip the matchup.
final-summary.winner: Galactus leads, but Trigon has live branch equity

stat-trap.question: Can Trigon poison the battlefield before Galactus turns it into fuel?
stat-trap.example: Galactus' better averages matter mostly on neutral ground. Once the battlefield shifts under Trigon's domain logic, raw numbers stop being enough.

tactical-board.lane: Trigon wins by keeping the battlefield poisonous. Galactus wins by turning poison into fuel.
tactical-board.subtitle: Demon versus Devourer

verdict-matrix.case_1: Galactus 8/10. Well-fed on neutral ground, he keeps the baseline answer set before corruption fully takes the map.
verdict-matrix.case_2: Galactus 6.5/10. Inside Trigon's realm the danger rises, but full reserves still let Galactus push the field back toward fuel.
verdict-matrix.case_3: Trigon 6/10. A starving Galactus is still dangerous on neutral ground, but each corruption cycle starts costing him far more.
verdict-matrix.case_4: Trigon 7.5/10. A starving Galactus inside Trigon's realm loses the clean normalization route, so field logic starts running the whole fight.

x-factor.mechanics: If the field stays demonic, Trigon stays live.
x-factor.implication: Whoever controls the battlefield's meaning controls the fight's branch logic.
x-factor.psychology: If the field becomes fuel, Galactus takes the fight back.

interpretation.line_1: Galactus owns the broader raw profile.
interpretation.line_2: Trigon stays dangerous because his value is nonlinear and field-dependent.

battle-dynamics.phase_1: Galactus starts stronger when space can be normalized and metabolized.
battle-dynamics.phase_2: Trigon rises as the battlefield behaves more like a demonic domain.
battle-dynamics.phase_3: The endgame depends on which field logic survives longer.
battle-dynamics.analysis: Galactus is strongest when space can be normalized and metabolized. Trigon rises when the field behaves more like a demonic domain.
